subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Form Accessibility Testing
description: A quick, practical guide to Form Accessibility Testing.

hook.text: A screen reader user tabs to an input field. It announces nothing—no label, no hint, no purpose.

buildup.text: Accessible forms require visible labels, programmatic association, error identification, and clear instructions.

discovery.text: Every input needs a label element linked by 'for' attribute. Placeholder text alone is not a valid label.

twist.text: Error messages must identify the field and describe the error. 'Invalid input' tells the user nothing useful.

climax.text: Adding proper labels, descriptions, and inline errors makes a 15-field form fully accessible.

punchline.text: Label every field. Describe every error. Leave no input anonymous.

quiz.question: Why is placeholder text not a valid label?
options: It disappears when the user starts typing, removing context
